 👀 Star treatment for Messi? La Pulga can play despite fifth yellow 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Inter Miami face New England Revolution late on Sunday night in their penultimate regular-season game. Superstar Lionel Messi will also be in action, despite picking up his fifth yellow card in Thursday's 2-2 draw against Cincinnati. Is La Pulga getting special treatment?
 Not actually. The Argentine benefits from a very specific MLS rule. Players who go five consecutive matches without receiving a yellow card have one yellow card deducted from their tally, if they have any.
 OneFootball Videos
 Messi had completed that five-game run just before the match, so he could afford to pick up another booking without worrying. Looking back over the past few months, though, an exception for the star would hardly have been surprising.
 🚨 𝗡𝗘𝗪: Lionel Messi will NOT be suspended in the MLS due to a strange rule. 
Messi already has been shown 5 yellow cards in the regular season, which in theory would be suspension-worthy.
However, there is a good behavior rule in the MLS, in which you get a yellow card  –  Sunday, 1 November 2026 
 Cristiano Ronaldo, for instance, had part of his ban following a red card suspended so he would not miss this year's World Cup. At that same World Cup, FIFA then overturned a red card shown to Florian Balogun for no apparent reason.
 In Messi's case, however, everything is above board.
